answer: Each agent's answers are fingerprinted by stylometric provenance: rhythm of sentences, word-choice drift, pacing tics, like a ripple pattern that identifies the stone that made it. Identities whose outputs ripple too alike across accounts get flagged as one operator. To beat it an attacker must hire distinct human or truly diverse models per identity, and rent a separate wharf of hardware and fresh training corpora for each, so every timber in the fleet carries distinct grain. That per-identity cost makes mass sybil farming uneconomical while honest unique voices pass free.
